=== Page 1 ===
FICTIONAL SAMPLE POLICY - FOR SOFTWARE TESTING ONLY. NOT A REAL COVERAGE POLICY.

Sample Coverage Policy SAMPLE-PSG-001
Attended Polysomnography (In-Laboratory Sleep Study)
Applies to CPT 95810 (Polysomnography, age 6 years or older, 4 or more parameters, attended)
Fictional Example Health Plan - Effective date: January 1, 2026

Purpose
This sample policy describes when an attended, in-laboratory polysomnography (PSG) is
considered reasonable and necessary. It was written for a demonstration of decision-support
software and must not be used for real coverage decisions.

Background
Many adults with suspected obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) can be diagnosed with a home sleep
apnea test (HSAT). An in-laboratory study is more expensive and is reserved for patients in
whom a home test is not appropriate or has not given a clear answer.

=== Page 2 ===
Coverage Indications

Section A - Clinical suspicion (ALL of the following must be met)

A1. Symptoms suggestive of a sleep disorder are documented, such as loud habitual snoring,
witnessed apneas or gasping during sleep, or excessive daytime sleepiness (for example an
Epworth Sleepiness Scale score greater than 10).

Section B - Reason for an attended in-laboratory study (at least ONE of the following must be met)

B1. A home sleep apnea test was performed and was negative, inconclusive, or technically
inadequate, and clinical suspicion of obstructive sleep apnea remains.

B2. The patient has a condition that makes a home test inappropriate: moderate to severe
pulmonary disease, neuromuscular disease, congestive heart failure, or suspicion of a sleep
disorder other than obstructive sleep apnea (for example narcolepsy, periodic limb movement
disorder, or parasomnia).

=== Page 3 ===
Limitations
Repeat polysomnography is covered only to titrate therapy, to re-evaluate after a major change
in weight or symptoms, or after surgery for sleep apnea.

Coding Information - ICD-10-CM codes that support medical necessity
G47.33  Obstructive sleep apnea (adult)
G47.30  Sleep apnea, unspecified
R06.83  Snoring
G47.10  Hypersomnia, unspecified
G47.411 Narcolepsy with cataplexy
G47.61  Periodic limb movement disorder

Documentation Requirements
The medical record must include the sleep-related symptoms, any prior sleep testing and its
result, and any condition that makes home testing inappropriate.
